title: Why modulo hashing collapses when a server leaves
description: Four keys, four servers, one failure. The keys did not move — the mapping moved out from under them, and every lookup misses at once.

nodes.label: All four keys moved
nodes.sublabel:
Removing 1 of N servers remaps
about (N−1)/N of all keys.
4 servers → 75%. 10 → 90%.

steps.text: Four servers become three. The divisor in hash(key) % N changes, so every key is recomputed against a different modulus — and in this example all four land somewhere new.
The data is still in the cache tier; the cluster just no longer looks for it in the right place. Every subsequent lookup misses.
Those misses fall through to the database — which now absorbs the entire read load of the system, at the exact moment you are already one server down. A routine node failure has become an outage.
